plan_a_advantages: Includes tempo runs to improve lactate threshold.
Incorporates hill workouts for strength and power development.
Offers a greater variety of workout types (long, hills, tempo, easy) leading to more well-rounded development.
Higher total training volume (565 minutes vs 489) may be beneficial for continued progress, assuming the athlete is recovering well.
plan_b_advantages: Simpler structure might be easier to follow and adhere to.

reasoning: Plan A appears to be the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans incorporate long runs and rest days, Plan A includes a wider variety of workouts – hills, tempo runs, and varying distances of easy runs – which is crucial for developing speed and strength on trails. Plan B focuses heavily on long, easy runs, which are important for building endurance but may not be sufficient to improve speed. The inclusion of tempo runs in Plan A specifically targets lactate threshold, a key factor in faster running, and the hill workouts build strength and power needed for trail running.
